title: Computational Advantage in Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks: Myth or Reality?
problem: Hybrid Quantum Neural Networks (HQNNs) are proposed for enhanced computational performance, but it is unclear whether quantum layers provide genuine computational advantage over classical models when both scale to handle increasing problem complexity.
motivation: HQNNs are gaining attention in QML, but fundamental questions remain unanswered about their practical computational efficiency vs classical networks, limiting informed architectural decisions in NISQ era.
method: Comprehensive benchmarking of classical networks at increasing problem complexity identifies efficiency-optimal baselines. HQNNs (simulated on classical hardware) are systematically compared by measuring FLOP scaling and parameter growth rates as problem complexity increases (10 to 110 features), revealing architectural scaling efficiency differences.
key_novelty: First systematic analysis showing HQNNs scale more efficiently in FLOPs (+53.1% vs +88.1% for classical) and parameters (+81.4% vs +88.5%) with problem complexity, demonstrating computational advantage despite simulation overhead.
contributions: Comprehensive benchmarking framework for classical models at increasing problem complexity.
Systematic comparison of HQNN vs classical network FLOP and parameter scaling.
Evidence that HQNNs provide more scalable, resource-efficient solutions for complex problems in NISQ era.

metrics.other: HQNN: 53.1% FLOP increase (10->110 features); Classical: 88.1%; HQNN parameter growth 81.4% vs 88.5% classical

limitations: Uses classical simulation of quantum layers (NISQ limitation), so does not evaluate on actual quantum hardware.
primary_theme: computational efficiency of hybrid quantum neural networks
